First, we rewrite the denominator using $1-{cos}^{2}⁡x={sin}^{2}⁡x.$

$$
\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}=\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{1-{cos}^{2}⁡x}
$$

Next, we factor the denominator as difference of squares, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{1-{cos}^{2}⁡x} & =\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}{\cancel{(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)} \\  & =\frac{1}{1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$
